messages.subject: Replicating Millsap & Yun-Tein (2004)
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to replicate the results of Millsap & Yun-Tein (2004) "Assessing factorial invariance in ordered-categorical measures" in Multivariate Behavioral Research using lavaan. Particularly, Tables 3, 5, and 7. 

The good news is that I can replicate their invariance findings in lavaan. However, it seems that I can't recover my parameters and I am wondering if maybe my data-generating mechanism was incorrectly specified or if even with n = 10,000 with ordered-categorical factor models I shouldn't except to recover my parameters. 

My R script is here: https://github.com/cddesja/lavaan-reproducible/blob/master/millsap2004-FIorderedCategorical.R

Thanks!
Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Replicating Millsap & Yun-Tein (2004)
parts: I can replicate their invariance findings in lavaan. However, it seems that I can't recover my parameters

I think this is because you are not fitting the same models to your data as they did, although your models might be statistically equivalent to their models (which would explain why you find the same "invariance findings", if that means the same model fit statistics).  For example, Millsap & Tein did not freely estimate their thresholds, which is what lavaan does by default in the models you ran.  Instead, Millsap & Tein fixed some thresholds to identify other model parameters.  You can (still?) find some example lavaan scripts here that fit Millsap & Tein's models, and they are the models currently fit by the measurementInvarianceCat() function in the semTools package, although that will change in the future.

http://sunthud.com/catInvariance.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Replicating Millsap & Yun-Tein (2004)
parts: Unfortunately, that link (sunthud.com) seems to be broken.

I attached the files that used to be there.  There are examples in Mplus and lavaan, for binary and 5-category data.  They specify the models suggested by Millsap & Tein (2004), but those specifications lead to frequent convergence issues with R's optimizer (that lavaan uses to find estimates).  

Furthermore, Millsap & Tein's advice was just a very nuanced special case, where their goal was to establish identification constraints in the configural model that would allow every type of parameter (except intercepts) to be freely estimated.  That is unnecessary because fixed factor means/variances can be freed in all but one group when equality constraints on measurement parameters are imposed, and the use of theta parameterization is not even relevant when one is uninterested in testing strict invariance. 

Wu & Estabrook (2016) more thoroughly illuminated the identification issues, and provided very different, much more general advice (namely, with 4+ categories, constrain thresholds first, then loadings, intercepts, and residuals as you would with continuous data).  With binary data, you can't separately identify most types of measurement parameter, so it only makes sense to start with the default configural model in lavaan, then constrain loadings and thresholds simultaneously (freeing total/residual variances in all but 1 group will happen by default when using the cfa() function).  Here is another thread where I discussed it in this forum (also on SEMNET):

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/7sglArLoIno/xMcJpNufBAAJ
Somewhat related, I am curious if anyone has an R script for examining measurement invariance with dichotomous items for lavaan?
I can provide the error, code, and some data if that would be helpful
That always helps to locate the actual problem.
but I'd prefer to use lavaan directly to test measurement invariance.

It is wise to specify these models ourselves, so we (learn to) understand what we are doing.  Automated routines only work in simple cases, and understanding why they fail always seems to require the same knowledge we would obtain by learning how to specify the model anyway :-)

Good luck,
